notes.title: Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel – Demo Launch
notes.content: [h2][/h2][p][b]Hi everyone,[/b][/p][p]I’m Raymond. About a year ago, I started [i]Revolving Gear Studios[/i] to finally try my hand at making video games full-time. I’ve been a hobbyist developer for years, and I always dreamed of building something bigger and more focused. That’s where this new Action RPG was born: [b]Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel[/b].[/p][p]The [b]Under a Desert Sun[/b] name might sound familiar — it comes from a small VR project I made years ago. I loved the world-building so much that I realized there were still plenty of stories left to tell in that universe.[/p][p]Why an Action RPG, you might ask? Before starting anything, I thought long and hard about what my first studio project should be. I kept coming back to the games that shaped my childhood: LAN parties with friends, playing [i]Diablo[/i] or [i]Titan Quest[/i] until sunrise, fueled by coffee and cola. Honestly, I was always more focused on saving the world, while my friends were all about the loot… :P In the end, I couldn’t think of a better reason to make a game than to follow my heart.[/p][p]So here we are! [b]This demo is an early, polished slice of Act 1[/b] — a first taste of what’s to come, released a few weeks ahead of Steam Next Fest in October.[/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]What you’ll find in the demo:[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/d4f5cca674232ed4acf14fd6cbe953eaff3096fd.gif"][/img][/p][list][*][p]Fast-paced ARPG combat with two classes: Soldier & Adventurer[/p][/*][*][p]Local co-op support (up to 4 players)[/p][/*][*][p]A first look at the game’s 1930s pulp-adventure style, story, and atmosphere[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]What’s not here yet (but will be in Early Access):[/b][/h3][list][*][p]The final loot & inventory systems[/p][/*][*][p]Online co-op[/p][/*][*][p]Later Acts, additional classes, and the full skill card deck[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]Looking Ahead – Early Access & Beyond[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/d4441e31cb5be88180595009f6bba7ec68e14eeb.png"][/img][/p][p]I’ve chosen Early Access very deliberately — for me it isn’t a gimmick, it’s a necessity. I want to use it as it was meant to be: to find passionate players who want to help shape the game, and in full transparency, to help fund further development.[/p][list][*][p][b]Current status:[/b] Right now you have the demo. Later this year, the Early Access release will follow with the same two classes and the [i]whole of Act 1[/i].[/p][/*][*][p][b]The road ahead (next ~2 years):[/b] I’ll continue working full-time on the game, adding:[/p][list][*][p]Four more story Acts (main quest + sidequests)[/p][/*][*][p]3–4 additional classes, including at least 1 magic-focused character and 2 full melee characters[/p][/*][*][p]Online co-op[/p][/*][*][p]Full voice acting[/p][/*][*][p]And everything else you’d expect from a complete ARPG you can enjoy with friends[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]And I want to be transparent about our studio’s stance on pricing and content. I know that when you buy Early Access, you’re spending your hard-earned money — often money you also need for essentials in a world where everything has gotten more expensive. That means when you buy [b]Under a Desert Sun[/b], you will get a [b]complete game[/b].[/p][list][*][p]No paid cosmetics[/p][/*][*][p]No seasonal passes that demand constant reinvestment[/p][/*][*][p]No microtransactions hidden in the corner[/p][/*][/list][p]The only possible extra cost in the future would be for proper expansions (DLCs), and those will always add substantial content: a new story Act, at least one new class, and a new set of items for every class.[/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]One last thing[/b][/h3][p]This demo is a work-in-progress, but it’s already playable and fun — and I’d really like to hear what you think. Leave feedback, tell us what parts you enjoyed, and if you feel like it, leave a review. Early impressions matter a lot as we head toward Next Fest, but most of all they help me understand what’s working and what still needs love.[/p][p]Thanks for giving this first adventure under the desert sun a try.[/p][p]– [b]Raymond @ Revolving Gear Studios[/b][/p]

notes.title: Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel - progression update
notes.content:
[p][b]Hello Seekers,[/b][/p][p]I thought it was a good moment to highlight some fresh progress! Development continues at full speed, starting with new environments and further work on the main quest. As some of you in the Discord already know, I use the main quest as a way to push myself to build new systems. I'm now at the point where everything leading up to the final moments of the main quest is functional—both tech-wise and, for the most part, art-wise.[/p][p]That means it was time to move the story forward again, which in turn forced me to create new areas, enemies, and gameplay features. One such feature is an improved [b]day and night system[/b], with smoother lighting transitions and smarter particle effects that fade out instead of abruptly disappearing. Below you'll find a quick idea of the new day/night features and a few in-editor screenshots showing the early stages of these new zones.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="W8fBpR4LRIY;full"][/previewyoutube][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/98681fabc5451329fa38a12406b8b82819de5a14.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/d4345efc8b2f50bf2f8ad3fd06a0145ef4d8c1ac.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/fc8caccf66faf6037f19803c5d2e466e21a1f55d.png"][/img][/p][p]Creating these new areas also meant designing [b]new enemy types[/b]—specifically ones that shoot projectiles! From Nazis who fire bullets to arcane mummies casting magical bolts, I needed to build the underlying tech. To get that going, I set up a test using our trusty mummy as a prototype. This allowed me to develop the full system: bullets, shooting and casting animations, and proper hit detection.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="UoC7sk9P1rg;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Naturally, new areas also bring [b]more destructibles[/b]. And let’s be honest—breaking stuff in an ARPG is just fun. (As you can see from me thrashing around... purely professional testing, of course 😏)[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="r_o0UvIZ_DE;full"][/previewyoutube][p]On the technical side, [b]Steam Deck optimization remains a major goal[/b]. The game currently runs at a stable 45 FPS on Deck [i]without[/i] any upscaling like FSR—so you get a clean image and native visuals. To get there, I’ve upgraded several systems under the hood. Particle systems now fade naturally, enemy spawning uses pooled and distance-aware logic, and we've improved object [b]occlusion and visibility handling[/b] to keep things smooth when off-screen. These changes help across all platforms but especially make the Deck experience strong.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Join the [url="https://discord.gg/g5fK7Df"]Discord[/url][/b] for daily development discussions and behind-the-scenes previews.
And if you like what you see—[b][url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3273880/Under_a_Desert_Sun_Seekers_of_the_Cursed_Vessel/"]wishlist the game on Steam[/url][/b] to support the journey![/p]

notes.title: Performance Update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/0dbb010153a6582344408a76138adebabfd291d6.gif[/img]

Performance is key in a game like this. The Steam Deck is a prime target for testing, and beta revealed that enemies’ individual search-and-behavior loops were impacting performance. A full AI overhaul merged those cycles under a single “Mother” controller (yes, a nod to Alien’s onboard computer), unlocking (as you can see in the small vid above):

A stable 45 FPS on Deck—no FSR or other upscalers needed

Dramatically reduced CPU load during the wildest firefights

Rock-steady frame pacing even in the most demanding areas

Cracking this “Mother” system feels like mastering the more difficult parts of gamedesign. It is a truly proud achievement that brings the project right on target for Deck performance. More polish is coming—stay tuned!

notes.title: Developer Update: Skill System Progress
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45534103/7e15d0657de73b13dc6d425c1a7b26fe49a1ce14.gif[/img]
Hi everyone! I’ve been working on further developing the skill system for the two playable classes currently in Under a Desert Sun: Seekers of the Cursed Vessel.

The goal is to give players meaningful choices through a layered approach to character customization:

On the right side of the screen, you'll find a classic Diablo II-style skill tree—both in appearance and philosophy. It’s deliberately old-school: no free respecs, so each decision matters and helps shape a distinct build.

Complementing that is a more flexible card slot system, which lets you adjust your playstyle on the fly. These cards introduce powerful modifiers and unique mechanics that can significantly alter your approach to combat and exploration.

The interaction between the two systems should create exciting variety. For example, one skill card available to the Adventurer disables rifle usage but unlocks the ability to dual wield pistols, enabling faster, close-range aggression.

The footage included in this update shows the player selecting a Frost or Burn bullet skill card—activating elemental bullets that apply freezing or burning effects to enemies on hit. This is just one of many ways skill cards can evolve your character’s abilities.
